result.question: We filtered the oil on Transformer 1 at site MAIN in early January, and I need a clean pre-filtration baseline to compare against. Pull the hydrogen, methane, ethylene, acetylene and co readings for every oil sample taken in the two months before 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000. Give me the min, max and mean of each gas over that pre-January period, and the average daily rise in ppm/day for hydrogen and acetylene. Then tell me by what percentage each gas is lower in the latest sample than in that baseline, so I can judge how much the filtration is masking the fault gases.
result.answer:
I can't build the baseline you asked for: Transformer 1 at MAIN has no oil-sample records before 2024-01-15.

- I searched 2023-11-15 up to (but not including) 2024-01-15 for hydrogen, methane, ethylene, acetylene and CO, and got 0 records back.
- The full telemetry history is only 5 daily samples, from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19. The very first record is at exactly 2024-01-15T00:00, the cutoff you gave, so none of it falls in the pre-filtration window.

That means I can't give you min, max or mean for that period, the average daily rise in hydrogen or acetylene, or how far the latest sample sits below the baseline. Making those numbers up from post-filtration data would hide exactly the masking you're trying to measure.

**Readings that do exist (all after the early-January filtration):**

| Gas | Min | Max | Mean | Latest (2024-01-19) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen (H₂) | 2800 | 2950 | 2869.0 | 2850 |
| Methane (CH₄) | 7200 | 7406 | 7331.2 | 7400 |
| Ethylene (C₂H₄) | 16500 | 16700 | 16626.8 | 16650 |
| Acetylene (C₂H₂) | 6 | 8 | 7.0 | 7 |
| CO | 30 | 35 | 32.4 | 32 |

Over these 5 days, hydrogen and acetylene show no clear trend, just scatter from one day to the next. Even after filtering, hydrogen, methane and ethylene are still very high, which fits an active thermal fault. So the filtration hasn't stopped the fault gases coming back.

**To get a real baseline:** use the lab DGA reports from before the filtration (Nov–Dec 2023), or ask whoever runs the historian whether older samples were archived somewhere else. Once you have those numbers, I can work out the baseline statistics, the ppm/day rise and the percentage drops.
